Meta.title: LTID | Turning the world's farms into a digital cooperative
Meta.description: Long Term Industrial Development (LTID) is building a digital agricultural cooperative that brings finance, distribution and AI to farmers in developing countries.
Meta.ogTitle: LTID — A digital cooperative for fair farming worldwide

Hero.subtitle: Finance × distribution × AI. Fair returns and lasting growth for farmers in developing nations.
Hero.marquee: FINANCE × DISTRIBUTION × AI  ·  DIGITAL COOPERATIVE  ·  TOKYO → BENGUET → ASIA → AFRICA  ·

Problem.title: When a retailer pays 100, the farmer receives 20–30.
Problem.lead: Farming nations, yet farmers are stuck on both capital and market access. Most of the value they grow never reaches them.
Problem.waffleCaption: The retail price, drawn as 100 squares

rows.title: No access to credit
rows.body: There are no banks in rural areas, and collateral reviews take months to a year. To buy seed and fertiliser, farmers borrow at punishing rates.

rows.title: No price visibility
rows.body: Routes to market and trading prices stay with the intermediaries. Farmers cannot know what their harvest is truly worth.

rows.statLabel: Needed per season (average income is about ¥200k)
rows.title: Not enough capital
rows.body: The money is needed before the harvest. Without it, equipment sits unused and some farmers give up farming altogether.

Problem.source: Source: Philippine Department of Agriculture statistics; Research Development Extension survey (as cited on FUNDINNO)

Solution.title: The role Japan's agricultural co-ops play, delivered digitally to the world.
Solution.lead: Finance, distribution and a fair price. In countries with no cooperative, a smartphone becomes the cooperative.

pillars.title: Agricultural finance
pillars.body: Fast, low-cost loans for seed, fertiliser and equipment, underwritten by AI credit scoring instead of land collateral.

pillars.title: Food value chain
pillars.body: Crop purchasing and buyer matching end to end, built with local intermediaries and their market know-how, not against them.

pillars.title: AI dynamic pricing
pillars.body: Highly accurate vegetable price prediction, giving farmers and buyers a transparent, fair price.

Solution.patent: Each technology is patent-pending in Japan and internationally

How.title: From loan to delivery, in a single app.

steps.title: AI judges credit, loans arrive fast
steps.body: Accuracy improves as borrower data grows. No collateral: start small, then scale loan sizes step by step.

steps.title: AI predicts a fair price and finds the buyer
steps.body: Dynamic pricing from supply, demand and market signals, so farmers finally see what their crop is worth.

steps.title: Ride-share logistics, safely
steps.body: Truck owners are matched with farmers. Photos at dispatch and arrival protect against loss, damage and fraud.

How.illustrative: * Graphics are illustrations of the service.

Impact.title: The service is already moving.
Impact.lead: Launched on 30 September 2021 in Benguet, Philippines. Within days, a waiting list formed.
Impact.disclaimer: Figures reflect information published in 2021–2022. Targets are the issuer's forecasts and are not guaranteed.

Partners.title: Built with governments, universities and industry.
Partners.lead: Working with public bodies, research institutions and companies in Japan and the Philippines to build a trustworthy foundation.
Partners.licence: Holds a lending licence in the Philippines

Roadmap.title: From the Philippines to Asia and Africa.
Roadmap.lead: The same problem exists across the world. We will carry a proven model to each new market.

steps.body: Live with vegetable farmers. Equipment-finance talks with a major manufacturer are underway.
Rice, corn and other staples. Preparing crop insurance, equipment sharing, food banks and more.
Expanding to India and Mozambique in East Africa: the digital cooperative as a global standard.

Roadmap.foodLoss: Cutting food loss is a core theme too: low-cost insulation for transport and re-circulating unsold produce.

Team.title: A global team in finance and technology.
Team.lead: Megabank new-business experience combined with strength in AI and app development.

members.name: Mariya Yokota
members.bio: Led Sony's broadcast and professional equipment business, with postings in Germany, London and Beijing, covering Eastern Europe, the Middle East, Africa and China. Former President of SFI Leasing.

members.name: Masayuki Fujimoto
members.bio: Head of Services & Solutions at Standard Chartered Bank, Tokyo branch (as of 2022). 15+ years in banking across technology operations, digital transformation, automation, technology risk and cyber security. Holds CISA, CISM, CRISC and other certifications. Director since December 2020.
